correctness.summary: The L'Huilier-Heron formulas reduce area to a symmetric product of three triangle-inequality slacks. Under fixed perimeter and Q those slacks have fixed first and second moments. Strict convexity of the derivative of log tan(t/2) or log tanh(t/2) forces all interior extrema to have two equal slacks; an exact convexity comparison orders the two branches, while the positive-octant boundary gives the sharp Q/p^2=1/8 transition to zero infimum.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Svrtan--Veljan (2012) gives non-Euclidean Finsler-Hadwiger inequalities but not complete fixed-(p,Q) area slices. Bogosel (2025) gives the exact Euclidean perimeter-area-Q diagram, which is explicitly excluded from novelty. Targeted searches did not locate the spherical or hyperbolic two-sided profiles, their universal 1/8 transition, or the interval-realization statement.

value.summary: The result upgrades known one-sided non-Euclidean Finsler-Hadwiger estimates to a complete sharp fixed-deficit area profile, classifies both isosceles extremal families, identifies the exact degeneracy threshold, and provides a direct constant-curvature analogue of the recently completed Euclidean diagram.

limitations: The spherical theorem assumes minor-arc geodesic triangles with perimeter below 2pi.
The stated unit-curvature formulas require scaling for other constant curvatures.
The asymmetry variable is the Euclidean quadratic side deficit Q.
The Euclidean exact profile is prior work and is not a novelty claim.
Equivalent older non-Euclidean formulations under different variables remain a residual originality risk.
